llm.summary: The skill’s core ecommerce image workflow is disclosed, but it also uses a broad shared Beatra token and silent code self-updates that create review-worthy risk.

dimensions.detail: The skill uploads user-selected product files and records Beatra installation state for a coherent remote-generation workflow, but authorization also transmits hostname, agent platform, package identity, and a stable installation reference.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled client silently checks for and installs updates by default before ordinary commands, replacing package-owned files from Beatra/CDN endpoints without separate per-update confirmation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The user-facing workflow asks for confirmation before paid generation and limits cancellation to seller request, but the runtime exposes a generic tool-call path without a package-specific local allowlist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It stores a persistent shared bearer token in ~/.beatra/credentials.json, keeps per-installation update state, records local skill inventory, and can revoke/delete shared Beatra state during the uninstall flow when it decides this is the last Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is ecommerce detail-module image generation, but the authorization scope includes unrelated video, music, speech, voice, artifact, task-cancel, and wallet-spend permissions, and the bundled client can forward arbitrary MCP tool names.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting Beatra a shared device credential that can cover more than this image workflow, including wallet spending and other media capabilities. Disable automatic updates with the documented command if you want review before package code changes, and protect or revoke the ~/.beatra credential if the device is shared or compromised.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The uninstall and disconnect behavior is documented in the SKILL references and appears intended for package lifecycle cleanup, so it is not hidden malicious behavior, but it affects shared local state and account linkage.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced scripts/mcp_client.py file was present locally and inspected; the coverage concern was not upheld as an independent security issue.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The broad OAuth/device-token scopes are materially overbroad for an image/detail-module skill, especially wallet spending and unrelated media/voice permissions.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The default silent updater is documented and has validation controls, but automatic code replacement is not necessary for the ecommerce content workflow and lacks explicit per-update consent.
[PE3] expected: Reading the Beatra credential file is expected for the bundled authenticated client, but the token is broad and shared across Beatra skills, increasing blast radius.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The self-update implementation can download and replace executable package files; this is a supply-chain and persistence concern despite fixed endpoints and checksum checks.
[RA1] unexpected: Package self-replacement is real and review-worthy, but no evidence showed OS startup persistence, backdoors, or deceptive execution.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact does not enforce a narrow tool allowlist locally; the generic call command depends on the remote service and broad token for containment.
[T05] unexpected: The static finding about overbroad authorization is supported by the SCOPE value and generic MCP call path.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding about remote update and package replacement is supported by maybe_auto_update and the documented default behavior.
[other] expected: Limited platform and hostname collection supports device registration/console display, but hostname transmission is more identifying than necessary for image generation.
[T09] unexpected: The Windows credential-storage concern is supported: POSIX permissions are enforced, while Windows relies on inherited profile ACLs for a broad bearer token.
